title: Custom Sequence money-management demo (EMA/candle reversal filter)
entry_long: candle ID2 body>=5pips (min body filter), ID2 bearish then ID1 bullish reversal whose body exceeds half of ID2 body (signal_level = ID2 body/2)
entry_short: mirror: ID2 bullish body>=5pips, ID1 bearish reversal body exceeds half of ID2 body
exit: no SL/TP shown in constants block; EA displays running MaxDD via equity-balance calc, no explicit close rule narrated
escalation_cap: unspecified (Custom Sequence table 2x,3x,5x,8x... of base lot on loss, reset to base on win; no lot cap block shown)
buildon_idea: add a Volume Upper Limit cap block on the custom-sequence lot output before deploying; the underlying reversal-candle entry could be tested standalone with fixed lot to isolate entry edge from the sequence risk
novelty_note: tutorial focus is the FXDreema built-in Custom Sequence MM block (asymmetric loss-recovery table) vs classic Martingale ratio; entry logic is generic candlestick reversal

title: Custom Sequence MM with EMA200+RSI+volume-confirmed engulfing entry
entry_long: price above EMA200; bearish ID2/bullish ID1 engulfing with ID1 tick-volume > ID2 volume; RSI7 < 30 (oversold)
entry_short: mirror: price below EMA200; bullish ID2/bearish ID1 engulfing with ID1 volume > ID2 volume; RSI7 > 70 (overbought)
exit: SL 300 pips, TP 500 pips per trade; Custom Sequence lot resets to base on win
escalation_cap: none (sequence table 2,3,5,8,13,21x of base 0.01 lot on consecutive loss; only guard is account-level cut-loss)
buildon_idea: add a hard Volume Upper Limit lot cap (sequence currently unbounded except by -1000 money cut-loss/Terminate); test flat-lot version of the volume-confirmed engulfing entry to verify standalone edge before re-adding the martingale table
novelty_note: adds tick-volume confirmation to engulfing entry (ID1 volume > ID2 volume) which is less common than plain body-size engulfing; account-level $ cut-loss with Terminate (not restart) is a distinct safety pattern

title: Multigroup scalping EA with EMA-filtered engulfing entry and hedge ("Hing") overflow system
entry_long: EMA3>EMA8>EMA200 (uptrend alignment) at ID1; bullish engulfing (ID2 bearish, ID1 bullish, body ID1>ID2); optional RSI<30 filter
entry_short: mirror: EMA3<EMA8<EMA200 downtrend; bearish engulfing; optional RSI>70 filter
exit: close-group at $5 profit (Close Money); no SL/TP on individual orders
escalation_cap: 5.0 lots (Volume Upper Limit); grid distance also doubles (100->200->400->800 pips) each add via lot-X=2 multiplier
buildon_idea: already capped at 5 lots + Max Order 30 + $3000 cut-loss on $10k; once capped-martingale exceeds 30 orders it opens an opposite-direction hedge ("Hing") to slow drawdown — worth isolating the Hing overflow mechanism as a standalone DD-tamer for other grid EAs
novelty_note: the 30-order overflow hedge (opens opposite-direction basket once grid depth hit, rather than just stopping) is a distinct DD-slowing technique worth cataloging separately from the base martingale grid

title: Multigroup scalping EA, engulfing+70%-body-ratio filter, step-wise lot add
entry_long: EMA8>EMA18>EMA200 alignment; pullback+bounce bullish engulfing where opposing (down) candle body < 70% of the up candle body; optional RSI7<30 (Scalping Mode off)
entry_short: mirror alignment/engulfing with down-candle body<70% of up-candle body; optional RSI7>70
exit: close-group money target scales with open-position count (close_money formula = base + f(count)); no fixed SL/TP, ATR-scaled trailing stop after 2+ orders
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step (C order B/S=5); Max Order 50, optional Save/Cut-loss mode
buildon_idea: already lot-capped and step-add (not doubling); the position-count-scaled close-money formula (avoid closing many orders at a fixed small $ target) is a reusable technique to test on other high-frequency grid EAs
novelty_note: the 70%-body-ratio filter on the opposing candle (reversal must be decisively larger than pullback candle) and the count-scaled close-money formula are both moderately novel refinements over plain engulfing+grid

title: Gold Robot EA: Williams %R oversold/overbought + doji reversal, ATR-trailing exit
entry_long: price>EMA200; WPR<-80 (oversold); bullish doji at ID1 (lower wick>upper wick, upper wick>body)
entry_short: mirror: price<EMA200; WPR>-20 (overbought); bearish doji at ID1
exit: ATR-scaled trailing stop (grid-distance*ATR-multiple), no fixed SL/TP; account-level cut-loss $500 on $2000 capital
escalation_cap: unspecified (Lot Plus increment mentioned as grid-add-on-loss but no cap value narrated in this transcript)
buildon_idea: pair with the sister video's explicit lot-cap/step logic (same EA family, EX193 second video) before deploying; the optional server-time filter (21:00-3:00) measurably cut cut-loss triggers from 8/yr to 4/2yr — worth testing as a universal session filter add-on
novelty_note: Williams %R is used instead of the more common RSI for oversold/overbought timing, explicitly noted by author as faster/more scalping-friendly; comment-block shows running MaxDD computed manually for MT5 (no native trade-statistics)

title: Gold Robot EA: Williams %R + doji + engulfing, step-wise lot add, dual-group cut-loss
entry_long: EMA3>EMA100 trend filter; WPR<-80 oversold; bullish doji (lower wick>upper wick>body) at ID1
entry_short: mirror: EMA3<EMA100; WPR>-20 overbought; bearish doji at ID1
exit: ATR-scaled trailing stop after 2+ orders; group closes on money-target scaled by open-count formula; no fixed SL/TP
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step; Max Order 50 (both buy/sell groups independent, cap trend vs reverse mode separately)
buildon_idea: already capped and step-add; author explicitly suggests testing buy-only vs sell-only vs both based on higher-TF trend bias to reduce DD — worth running that A/B as the build-on test
novelty_note: same WPR+doji concept as sister video but adds the count-scaled close-money formula and independent buy/sell group management; author explicitly frames it as sculping-suited due to WPR's faster response vs RSI

title: Gold Robot EA: doji + engulfing combo entry, EMA200 filter, ATR-trailing exit
entry_long: price>EMA200; bearish doji at ID2 (lower wick>upper wick>body, all bearish-shaped) then bullish engulfing at ID1 (body ID1>ID2)
entry_short: mirror: price<EMA200; bullish doji at ID2 then bearish engulfing at ID1
exit: ATR-scaled trailing stop after 2+ orders (grid_distance*ATR multiple); no fixed SL/TP; account-level cut-loss optional
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step; Max Order 50
buildon_idea: already lot-capped/step-add; author notes this combo (doji then confirming engulfing) produced fewer/cleaner entries than plain engulfing on 1min gold during a high-volatility month — worth isolating the doji-then-engulfing filter as a precision upgrade for EX192/EX193 entries
novelty_note: combining doji (indecision) immediately followed by confirming engulfing is a stricter 2-stage reversal filter than either pattern alone; author reports it survived December 2025's sharp swings with DD only 11%

title: Multi Group Scalping EA: pin-bar/doji reversal, rebalance close (%-of-balance profit target)
entry_long: ID2 bearish doji (lower wick>upper wick>body, 2x body-size filter vs ID2), ID1 bullish confirming candle body>=2x ID2 body; group-1 buy
entry_short: mirror doji/confirm logic for group-2 sell
exit: trend-follow mode closes at 1% of balance profit; reverse/recovery mode closes at 0.1% of balance profit (asymmetric %-of-equity targets, not fixed $); optional cut-loss mode force-closes a group at 50 orders
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step; Max Order 50 (cut-loss threshold)
buildon_idea: the balance-percentage profit target (1% trend-mode vs 0.1% recovery-mode, called "rebalance") scales targets with account size automatically — worth extracting as a reusable exit module independent of this EA's entry, and pairing with a hard lot cap test across more symbols
novelty_note: the %-of-balance dual profit target (asymmetric between trend-follow and recovery/reverse mode) is the most novel piece here — most sister EAs in this batch use fixed-$ close-money instead

title: Multigroup scalping EA: MACD divergence + engulfing confirmation + EMA trend filter
entry_long: MACD bullish divergence (built-in FXDreema block) on chosen signal TF; confirmed by bullish engulfing (ID2 bearish, ID1 bullish, body ID1>ID2); EMA8>EMA200 filter
entry_short: mirror: MACD bearish divergence + bearish engulfing + EMA8<EMA200 filter
exit: close-group at $5 profit; no fixed SL/TP; Max Order 15 acts as forced cut-loss (give up regardless of P&L once 15 orders open, sized for $1000 capital on 5min TF)
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step; Max Order 15 (tight, tuned to small $1000 account)
buildon_idea: MACD-divergence-confirmed-by-engulfing is a distinct entry filter from the batch's plain candlestick patterns — worth cross-testing on other symbols/TFs since divergence signals are typically lower-frequency/higher-quality; Max Order 15 is capital-sized (tune per account before reuse)
novelty_note: uses FXDreema's built-in MACD Divergence block (auto-draws price/MACD divergence lines) rather than manual indicator math — the divergence+engulfing double-confirmation is a step up in entry rigor vs plain-pattern EAs in this batch

title: Multigroup scalping EA: MACD divergence + engulfing, percentage-of-balance cut-loss
entry_long: MACD bullish divergence (built-in block) + confirming bullish engulfing (ID2 bearish, ID1 bullish, body ID1>ID2); price>EMA200
entry_short: mirror: MACD bearish divergence + bearish engulfing + price<EMA200
exit: close-group at $5 profit; no fixed SL/TP; combined-group cut-loss when both groups' unrealized P&L falls below -30% of current balance (percentage, not fixed $, per user request)
escalation_cap: 0.1 lots (Volume Upper Limit); +0.01 lot every 5-order step (no fixed Max Order in this variant — cut-loss is purely the 30%-of-balance combined check)
buildon_idea: the percentage-of-balance combined-group cut-loss (auto-scales with account size, checks both buy+sell groups together) is a reusable risk module worth pairing with sister EX195 video's fixed Max-Order cut-loss to compare which controls DD better across account sizes
novelty_note: same MACD-divergence+engulfing core as sister video but swaps the fixed-order-count cut-loss for a %-of-balance combined-group cut-loss, explicitly built at a student's request — a cleaner, account-size-agnostic risk control worth extracting
